courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Race, Sex, and Place in America
courses.description: This first-year seminar will expose students to the complex dynamics of race, ethnicity, and gender and how these have shaped the American city since 1945.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Writing Women in Modern China
courses.description: Compares the rhetoric of equality between the sexes presented by late Qing, May Fourth, and communist thinkers to perspectives on gender and society by 20th-century Chinese women writers. Honors version available.

source.text: WGST 56. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING. | ASIA 56 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Plantation Lullabies: Literature by and about African American Women
courses.description: This course introduces students to different ways of understanding plantation culture and how that culture persists today, using close reading strategies and gender analysis. The class will examine film, literature, music, and poetry.

source.text: WGST 64. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-PAST or FC-VALUES.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Growing Up Girl, Globally
courses.description: Course introduces students to literature by women from around the world, particularly stories of a girl's transition to womanhood. Close reading strategies are used to examine films, novels, and poetry.

source.text: WGST 66. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Sexuality and Salvation
courses.description: In Christianity and Islam, bodies populate the afterlife. What those bodies look like, how they act, what they feel, and who they engage with are subjects of contentious and long-standing debates. The various answers offered in these debates deeply affect Christian and Muslim responses to the body, sexuality, race, and gender in this life. This course examines how these two religious traditions' diversity of histories and ideas construct theories of identity.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Assumed Identities: Performance in Photography
courses.description: Uses photography and its aspects of role playing, performance, and documentation to understand the construction of identity. Looks at historical and contemporary photographers who use assumed identities to explore their changing identity roles and challenge society's stereotypes. Individual and group performance/photography projects working with still photography, video, and the Internet.

source.text: WGST 68. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-CREATE or FC-KNOWING.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Feminism and Food Justice
courses.description: This course will explore feminist perspectives on food justice. We will focus on the gendered labor of food production and current problems, including the role of agriculture in climate change and consumption patterns. Material will cover both historical and contemporary periods but focus on 20th and 21st century United States. Students will complete several short writing assignments, one interactive project, and a final project.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester. Honors version available.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Introducing Intersectionality: Gender, Race, Class, and Sexuality
courses.description: An interdisciplinary exploration of the intersections of gender, race, class, and sexuality in American society and internationally. Topics include work; sexuality; gender relations, and images of women in literature, art, and science; and the history of feminist movements. Course readings are drawn from the humanities and the social sciences. Honors version available.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Introduction to Sexuality Studies
courses.description: This course introduces students to the broad range of disciplinary perspectives used by the field of sexuality studies to study, teach, and create knowledge about human sexuality in various functions and forms.

source.text: WGST 111I. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-POWER, INTERDISCI.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Introduction to Sexuality Studies
courses.description: This course introduces students to the broad range of disciplinary perspectives used by the field of sexuality studies to study, teach, and create knowledge about human sexuality in various functions and forms.

source.text: WGST 111H. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-POWER, INTERDISCI.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Experiencing Latina/o America
courses.description: This Interdisciplinary course introduces tools and methods for learning about the "Latina/o American Experience." Using film, cultural products and technologies, it engages Latino/a and Latin American Studies, geography, and women's and gender studies to learn about, analyze, and reflect on the experience of peoples of Latin American ancestry across the Americas. Students may not receive credit for both LTAM 117I and IDST 117I .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Experiencing Latina/o America
courses.description: This Interdisciplinary course introduces tools and methods for learning about the "Latina/o American Experience." Using film, cultural products and technologies, it engages Latino/a and Latin American Studies, geography, and women's and gender studies to learn about, analyze, and reflect on the experience of peoples of Latin American ancestry across the Americas. Students may not receive credit for both LTAM 117I and IDST 117I .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Sex and Gender in Society
courses.description: Examination of the social differentiation between men and women. Attention to the extent, causes, and consequences of sexual inequality and to changes in sex roles and their impact on interpersonal relations.

source.text: WGST 124. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-POWER. | SOCI 124 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Iranian Women Writers
courses.description: This course introduces students to Iranian women's issues through their literary works. To contextualize, we will read articles and essays on the historical, cultural, social, political, and economic backgrounds. In order to approach these literary works in a more effective manner, we will also be reading various secondary materials.

source.text: WGST 127. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-GLOBAL. | ASIA 127 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Introduction to Gay and Lesbian Culture and Literature
courses.description: Introduces students to concepts in queer theory and recent sexuality studies. Topics include queer lit, AIDS, race and sexuality, representations of gays and lesbians in the media, political activism/literature.

source.text: WGST 140. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | ENGL 140 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women in United States History
courses.description: This course will survey the history of women, gender relations, and notions of sex difference in the United States from the colonial era to present times, with a special emphasis on women's varied experiences and expectations across divisions of class, race, and region. Key themes will include work, politics, citizenship, reproduction, sociability, and sexuality.

source.text: WGST 144. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | HIST 144 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender, Sexuality, and Social Justice in South Asia
courses.description: This course explores questions of ethics, justice, and inequality with respect to gender in modern South Asia. Each unit will probe a different aspect of social justice in order to understand the histories, politics, and expressive cultures of various disempowered communities. Intersections between gender and ethics, politics, sexuality, caste, class, and the environment will be studied in depth.

source.text: WGST 167. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | ASIA 167 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Introduction to Women and Music
courses.description: The role of women in performance, composition, patronage, and the music business across a wide range of repertories.

source.text: WGST 188. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | MUSC 188 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Africa
courses.description: Introduction to the study of gender and sexuality in African societies. Theoretical questions relating to the cross-cultural study of gender will be a primary focus. Topics include historical perspectives on the study of kinship and family in Africa and the impact of colonialism and other forms of social change.

source.text: WGST 200. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-KNOWING. | AAAD 200 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Introduction to Feminist Thought
courses.description: Introduces students to feminist theorizing on debates over gender-based oppression. Gives students tools to pursue academic work in women's studies and to understand the relationships among concepts, activism, and change. Required for majors. Strongly recommended for minors.

source.text: WGST 202. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, WGST 101 . | FC-KNOWING or FC-POWER.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Introduction to Latina Feminisms: Literature, Theory, and Activism
courses.description: Through a variety of texts that span the 20th and 21st centuries, students will be introduced to key concepts, figures, and movements in Latina feminisms. Emphasis will be placed on a diversity of historical and ethno-national perspectives as well as academic interdisciplinarity.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender and Spirituality
courses.description: The course is designed to introduce a variety of ways that gender is present in how we define, interpret, and engage the broad categories of the spiritual and spiritualities. Students will learn how to analyze how gender is portrayed by spiritual and religious traditions and reflect on the socially constructed nature of those encounters.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women and Politics
courses.description: A comparison of men and women as political actors at the mass and elite level in America. Topics considered include the "gender gap," the women's movement, abortion, and the Equal Rights Amendment.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women in the Middle Ages
courses.description: This interdisciplinary course examines representations of women, concepts of gender, and women's participation in the economic, political, religious, and cultural life of the Middle Ages. Discussion and texts in English.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Prehistoric Art
courses.description: A survey of prehistoric art in Africa, the Americas, Australia, and Europe.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Introduction to Gender and Communication
courses.description: Examines multiple relationships among gender, communication and culture. Explores how communication creates gender and shapes relationships and how communication reflects, sustains, and alters cultural views of gender. Honors version available.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Space, Place, and Difference
courses.description: Gender, race, and class are examined in terms of the spatial patterns of everyday life, regional patterns, and global patterns. (GHA)

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women in Contemporary Art: A Field Study
courses.description: This seminar will explore the lives and work of women in contemporary art through a combination of readings, films, interviews, studio visits with area artists, and visits to museums and galleries. We will engage questions of identity, gender, sexuality, politics, and cultural representation and how these affect the creativity, media, and final output of women artists.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender and Popular Culture
courses.description: This course examines the ways in which gender and sexual identities are represented and consumed in popular culture.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Identity in Transit: Performing the Self through Photography
courses.description: This course asks how gendered identity is shaped over time in relation to different cultural, social, and historical circumstances. Examines the practices of photographers who present themselves and others in assumed identities to comment on shifting social roles and challenge stereotypes. Students use photography to document performance and create self-portraits.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Introduction to Latina Literature
courses.description: This course will provide an introduction to Latina literature. We will read a variety of genres from a range of ethno-national perspectives and examine such topics as immigration, identity, mother-daughter relationships, and sexuality.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Motherhood: Politics and Representation
courses.description: This course focuses on how institutions and experiences of motherhood are shaped by race, ethnicity, gender, sexuality, class, and religion, giving particular attention to popular notions of ''good'' and ''bad'' mothers, explorations of maternal feelings, and examinations of mothering as gendered labor and care.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Rebel, Lover, Martyr: Gender and Sexuality in North and South Korean Screen Cultures
courses.description: This course introduces students to the history of North and South Korean film and television through the lens of gender and sexuality. In so doing, it explores the multiple forms of the Korean self and the diverse shapes that Korean identity has taken across the modern and contemporary eras.

source.text: WGST 237. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | KOR 237 , CMPL 237 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women in Greek Art and Literature
courses.description: Course examines law, religion, medicine, social practices, and ideologies in the lives of women in ancient Greece, from Homer to Hellenistic Egypt, using literature, art, and epigraphy. Honors version available.

source.text: WGST 240. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING. | CLAS 240 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women in Ancient Rome
courses.description: Course examines the life of women in ancient Rome, from the first beginnings of the organized community in Rome through the early Empire, a period of about 900 years. Also explores aspects of the lives of women in provinces governed by Rome. Honors version available.

source.text: WGST 241. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-PAST. | CLAS 241 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Sex and Gender in Antiquity
courses.description: Exploration of gender constructs, what it meant to be a woman or a man, in antiquity, as revealed in literary, historical, and archaeological sources. Readings from Homer, Euripides, Plato, Ovid, Virgil, Juvenal, Petronius, and other ancient authors.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Western Christianity
courses.description: An examination of the development of teachings on issues of gender and sexuality through the history of Western Christianity, with particular focus on contemporary controversies. Honors version available.

source.text: WGST 244. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | RELI 244 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender on the Musical Stage
courses.description: An exploration of gender on the musical stage in the past and present, with an emphasis on female-identified creators and characters, onstage and behind the scenes.

source.text: WGST 248. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | MUSC 248 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Intersectionality: Race, Gender, Sexuality, and Social Justice
courses.description: The first goal of this super course is to give students real tools for how to address multiple modes of difference and identity formations like race, gender, class, and sexuality.

source.text: WGST 249. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER. | AMST 248 , ENGL 248 , POLI 248 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: A Social History of Jewish Women in America
courses.description: This course examines the history and culture of Jewish women in America from their arrival in New Amsterdam in 1654 to the present and explores how gender shaped this journey.

source.text: WGST 253. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | AMST 253 , JWST 253 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women in the Visual Arts I
courses.description: This course analyzes the role of women in Western art as art producers and consumers of art and looks at how women have been represented.

source.text: WGST 254. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | ARTH 254 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Towards Emancipation? Women in Modern Europe
courses.description: This course examines and compares the situation of women in politics, the work force, society and family from the French Revolution to the new women's movement in the 1970s with a focus on Britain, France and Germany. One major theme is the history of the struggle for women's emancipation.

source.text: WGST 259. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | HIST 259 , EURO 259 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women and Sport
courses.description: A broad based perspective of women's participation in sport including history of participation, physiological differences, and socio-cultural influences including work, politics, family, economics, and gender roles and identity.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender, Sport, and Society
courses.description: An interdisciplinary exploration of how gender shapes participation, representation, and power in sport. Drawing from feminist, historical, scientific, and cultural perspectives, the course examines women's and gender-diverse experiences in athletics, policies like Title IX, and ongoing debates about embodiment, equity, and the gender binary in sport.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Literature and Gender
courses.description: Focused study of how issues of gender shape literary themes, characters, and topics, and the composition and reception of literary texts. Honors version available.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender in Russian History
courses.description: Traces the development of sexual identities and changes in masculine and feminine ideals from Tsarist Russia through the post-Soviet period with emphasis on politics, society, and popular culture.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Feminism and Political Theory
courses.description: Introduction to feminist theory and its implications for the study and practice of political theory. Topics: women in feminist critiques of the Western political tradition, schools of feminist political theory.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Black Women in America
courses.description: An examination of the individual and collective experiences of black women in America from slavery to the present and the evolution of feminist consciousness.

source.text: WGST 266. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | AAAD 232 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Introduction to Transgender Studies
courses.description: This course surveys the breadth of the field of transgender studies through an interdisciplinary lens. This course will outline trans history from 16th century to the present as well as current topics addressed by scholars in the field.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women in German Cinema
courses.description: Introduction to feminist aesthetics and film theory by the examination of the representation of women in German cinema from expressionism to the present. All materials and discussions in English. Previously offered as GERM/WGST 250.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Masculinities
courses.description: This class is an interdisciplinary study of masculinities as theorized by feminists and shaped by race, class, sexuality, gender identity, age, ability, and nationality. Meanings of masculinities will be addressed at multiple levels - historical, structural, cultural, and interpersonal - and in multiple sites - childhood, adolescence, the body, education, work, sports, popular culture, immigration, gender violence, and mass incarceration.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Moral and Philosophical Issues of Gender in Society
courses.description: A survey of feminist perspectives on topics such as the meaning of oppression, sexism and racism, sex roles and stereotypes, ideals of female beauty, women in the workplace, pornography, rape. Honors version available.

source.text: WGST 275. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | PHIL 275 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender and Culture
courses.description: Examines what it means to be male, female, and other gendered categories in different societies. Focus on institutions, groups, and individuals that both shape and challenge how gender is understood, organized, and enacted.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women in Science
courses.description: The role of women in scientific domains throughout history and a consideration of the status of women and men as scientists. The development of science as a cultural practice.

source.text: WGST 278. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES, RESEARCH. | ANTH 278 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women and Gender in Latin American History
courses.description: Examines the experiences of women and gender relations in Latin American societies from pre-Columbian times to the present, providing a new perspective on the region's historical development.

source.text: WGST 280. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | HIST 280 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender and Global Change
courses.description: Through a diverse set of texts, students will examine the role of armed conflict in forming United States empire in the 20th and 21st centuries. The course will also consider the gendered contradictions of freedom and historical embodiments of war and violence.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: African American Women in the Media
courses.description: This course will acquaint students with how African American women have been depicted (and depicted themselves) in 20th- and 21st-century media. The course will examine representations of African American women in several aspects of culture including film, art, print, television, theater, and music.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Special Topics in Women's Studies
courses.description: Topics are announced in advance and reflect the interest of the particular instructor. Each course will concern itself with a study in depth of some problem or issue in women's studies.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Special Topics in Women's and Gender Studies, FC-GLOBAL
courses.description: Topics are announced in advance and reflect the interest of the particular instructor. Each course will concern itself with a study in depth of some problem or issue in women's studies.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Language and Power
courses.description: This course provides an overview of language and power studies. Issues: sexist and sex-neutral language; languages of subcultures defined by gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity; hate speech; "politically correct" language.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women and the Law in Africa and the Middle East
courses.description: Explores women's and men's engagement with colonial and post-colonial legal systems with a focus on the 19th through 21st centuries. Topics include customary law, Islamic law, women's rights as human rights, disputation and conflict resolution. We will ask the question: "how does gender influence how women and men navigate legal systems?" Course previously offered as WMST 289.

source.text: WGST 313. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST. | HIST 313 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Sexuality and Salvation
courses.description: In Christianity and Islam, bodies populate the afterlife. What those bodies look like, how they act, what they feel are subjects of popular and scholarly contentious, long standing debates. The various answers that have been offered in these debates deeply affect Christian and Muslim responses to the body, sexuality, race, and gender in this life. This course examines how theories about sex, gender, and identity are constructed within two religious traditions' histories, ideas, and theories.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Encountering Art in the Unexpected: Borderlands and Story in Contemporary American Visual Art
courses.description: This course focuses on the contemporary art and social change movement. We will learn how to use site-specific and performative art interventions to make invisible borders, boundaries, and other issues visible and innovatively to create engaged and sustained dialogue.

source.text: WGST 325. | 3 Credits. | FC-CREATE or FC-GLOBAL. | AMST 325 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Middle East Women Writers
courses.description: We examine works written by Middle Eastern women. We will begin with reading speeches and short stories in the 1860s. We will focus on topics such as Middle Eastern women and feminism and the West; women and nationalism; women and colonialism; women and patriarchy; women, sexuality, and religion.

source.text: WGST 329. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER. | ASIA 329 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women's Health Activism in Twentieth Century America
courses.description: Course examines the history of women's health activism and advocacy in the 20th century United States. Course materials and discussions will trace the development of several women's health movements and causes, health activists' tactics and rhetoric, and the complex dynamic between lay activists and medical professionals.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: African Gender History
courses.description: Required preparation, at least one AAAD or WMST course. This course seeks to familiarize students with scholarly debates on the importance of gender as a category of analysis, while gaining a greater sense of the African past.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Leadership in Violence Prevention
courses.description: Examines interpersonal violence, the factors that enable it, and prevention strategies. The course examines violence on both individual and structural levels, considering perpetrators, victims/survivors, and bystanders and drawing upon the expertise of local organizers and service providers in the system of care.

source.text: WGST 340. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, WGST 101 . | FC-POWER, HI-SERVICE.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender and Film
courses.description: This course examines the representations of women in contemporary American film and also considers women as producers of film.

source.text: WGST 345. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING. | COMM 345 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Spitting in the Wind: "American" Women, Art, and Activism
courses.description: This course uses films, novels, and essays to engage with various notions of activism (as represented in art and social justice organizations) at play in hemispheric America.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Rahtid Rebel Women: An Introduction to Caribbean Women
courses.description: This course uses films, novels, and essays to move beyond sun, sand, and sex representations of Caribbean women to examine how they negotiate imperial and national definitions of their place.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: War and Gender in Movies
courses.description: The course examines and compares the images of war and gender that movies from different time periods and countries propagate and explores the different factors that influence these images and thereby the perception and recollection of war. Honors version available.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: American Women's History to 1865
courses.description: This course will explore women's experiences in America from 1500 to 1865. Topics will include the ways in which women have shaped American politics, economy, society, and culture.

source.text: WGST 354. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | HIST 355 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: American Women's History, 1865 to the Present
courses.description: This course will examine the changing lives of women in the United States after 1865: Their contribution to economy, society, cultural change, and political struggles.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, and Transgender Histories in the United States
courses.description: This course investigates the history of people who might today be defined as lesbian, gay, bisexual, or transgender (LGBT) in the United States. Key themes will include identity formation, culture, politics, medical knowledge, discrimination, and community.

source.text: WGST 360. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | HIST 361 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Asian American Women's Writing
courses.description: This course covers writings by Asian American women and examines issues of gender, race, and sexuality.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Mary in the Christian Tradition
courses.description: In certain eras, Mary has been more central to Catholic devotion than Christ. This course explores doctrine, liturgy, and popular devotion centering on the Virgin in medieval European Christianity, her impact on colonial religion in the New World, and her roles in Protestantism, Eastern Orthodoxy, and Islam. Honors version available.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Feminist Literary Theory
courses.description: Theories of feminist criticism in relation to general theory and women's writing. Honors version available.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Sexuality, Gender, and Public Policy
courses.description: Public policies affect men and women differently, and they participate differently in the policy-making process. This course examines several key areas of public policy, some expressly related to gender or sexuality and others that have significantly gendered impacts, organized around four themes: family, labor, body, and the world.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women of Color in Contemporary United States Social Movements
courses.description: This course will examine the role of women of color as grassroots activists, leaders, and thinkers in the new social and community movements of the postwar period.

source.text: WGST 368. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, WGST 101 . | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Race, Sexuality, and Disability in the History of Western Christianity
courses.description: Over time, Christian institutions and traditions have helped constitute contemporary narratives of race, sexuality, and disability in society. This course examines shifting definitions and specific case studies from the premodern era through to contemporary discourses and polemics in America. Honors version available.

source.text: WGST 370. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-POWER. | RELI 368 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women Mystics
courses.description: An investigation of the forms, characteristics, and variety of the mystical experiences of women in medieval and modern Christianity, with comparative consideration of women mystics and spiritual leaders in at least two other religious traditions.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Modern Women Writers
courses.description: The development of a women's literary tradition in the works of such writers as George Sand, George Eliot, Isak Dinesen, Colette, Virginia Woolf, Gertrude Stein, Marguerite Duras, Nathalie Sarraute, Marguerite Yourcenar.

source.text: WGST 373. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | CMPL 374 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Southern Women Writers
courses.description: The study of fiction, poetry, plays, and essays by Southern American women writers of the past 200 years, continuing to the present.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: History of Gender in America
courses.description: This course will explore how Americans from 1600 to the present have defined what is masculine and what is feminine and how they have constructed their identities around those definitions.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Almost Despicable Heroines in Japanese and Western Literature
courses.description: Authors' use of narrative techniques to create the separation between heroines and their fictional societies and sometimes also to alienate readers from the heroines. Austen, Flaubert, Ibsen, Arishima, Tanizaki, Abe.

source.text: WGST 380. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-GLOBAL. | CMPL 380 , ASIA 380 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women Writers: Brazil and Beyond
courses.description: Trajectory of women writers of the Portuguese-speaking world, with main focus on texts of the 20th and 21st century. Analysis of works within a social-historical and literary context.

source.text: WGST 381. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | PORT 382 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: African American Women's History
courses.description: The course covers the history of black women in the United States from the 18th century to the present. It deals with such themes as work, family, community, sexuality, politics, religion, and culture. Previously offered as HIST/WGST 569.

source.text: WGST 382. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | HIST 385 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Black Feminist Thought & the Speculative Imagination
courses.description: This class places transnational Black feminist thought in conversation with Black speculative fiction from across the diaspora, particularly emphasizing sci-fi and fantasy narratives set in dystopic or post-apocalyptic worlds. By reading these two traditions of writing together, we study how both genres theorize the potential sources of, responses to, and preventative measures against forms of political, social, and environmental catastrophe.

source.text: WGST 383. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | AAAD 388 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Comparative Studies in Culture, Gender, and Global Forces
courses.description: Examines participatory development theory and practice in Africa and the United States in the context of other intervention strategies and with special attention to culture and gender.

source.text: WGST 386. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, AAAD 101 and 130 . | AAAD 386 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: The International Politics of Sexual and Reproductive Health
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Takes a feminist political economy perspective on debates over current health issues of international concern, including abortion, population control, and sexually transmitted infections. Focuses on the United States, Mexico, and Kenya, as well as on international organizations and social movements.

source.text: WGST 388. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, WGST 101 . | FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Internship in Women's and Gender Studies
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. A supervised internship designed to provide experience working in organizations concerned with women's or gender issues. Must be arranged with a faculty advisor during the semester prior to the internship. See the department's website for important information.

source.text: WGST 393. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, WGST 101 . | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES, HI-INTERN.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Independent Reading and Research
courses.description: Permission of curriculum chair. Faculty supervison required. Independent reading and research. A student can repeat the course as long as they work on a different topic each time they enroll.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Special Topics in Women's and Gender Studies, FC-PAST
courses.description: Topics are announced in advance and reflect the interest of the particular instructor. Each course will concern itself with a study in depth of some problem or issue in women's studies.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Feminist Ways of Knowing
courses.description: This course has two main purposes. First, it will build on the work students have done in WGST 202 ; students will explore more deeply significant trends, key theoretical texts, and epistemological and methodological debates in feminist thought. Second, by emphasizing connections among theory, method, evidence, and analysis, it will prepare students for the senior capstone course in which they develop and carry out a major research project.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender, Sexuality, Empire and Asian Pacific America
courses.description: This advanced undergraduate course examines the diverse terms by which empire and sexuality have produced and reflected gender in Asian Pacific America. This seminar brings together two strains of politicized critical analysis: queer/feminist studies and postcolonial studies through the interdisciplinary standpoint of Asian American studies. Close readings are drawn from the social sciences, humanities, and arts.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Comparative Queer Politics
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Compares the histories, experiences, identities, and political struggles of sexual and gender minorities in Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and the Américas and at the United Nations.

source.text: WGST 410. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, WGST 101 . | FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Queer Theory and Religion
courses.description: This course examines the differing philosophical approaches in queer theory (psychoanalytic, cultural, transnational) in order to understand how scholars have incorporated discussions of sex, sexuality, gender, and race into their own work on religions.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Family and Gender in Early Modern China and Korea
courses.description: This course explores family and kinship in early modern China and Korea through the lens of gender and sexuality. In particular, it invites students to think beyond the bias that women in premodern East Asia were victims of patriarchy to understand their active participation in their world-making as well as their dynamic imagination and expression through writing, working, learning, loving.

source.text: WGST 418. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | ASIA 418 , HIST 418 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender Theory and the Study of Religion
courses.description: An examination of contemporary gender theory, with particular focus on its application to the study of religion.

source.text: WGST 424. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | RELI 424 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender and Performance: Constituting Identity
courses.description: Examines the culturally and historically variable ways in which individuals constitute themselves as cis- or transgendered subjects or nonbinary subjects, drawing upon extant expressive resources, modifying them, and expanding options available to others. Performance of self as the product of esthetically marked or unmarked, everyday actions.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Health in Socialist, Liberal, and Illiberal Upheavals
courses.description: This course examines the health ideals and outcomes produced by historical experiences of socialism, liberalism, and authoritarianism in the 20th and 21st centuries. Students will learn about anthropological frameworks examining health in political-economic and socio-cultural contexts. Cases will address reproductive and sexual health, infectious disease, and others.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: The Anthropology of Gender, Health, and Illness
courses.description: The course explores cultural beliefs, practices, and social conditions that influence health and sickness of women and men from a cross-cultural perspective.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender, Class, Race, and Mass Media
courses.description: The media play a critical role in the construction and contestation of ideas about gender, class, and race. Using a range of methods, students will analyze media messages past and present to understand how gender, race, and class influence media production and consumption.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Cultures and Politics of Reproduction
courses.description: This course takes a cross-cultural approach to understanding how reproduction and associated phenomena become arenas where political debates are played out, and where global and local social relations are contested.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Race, Class, and Gender
courses.description: Conceptualizations of gender, race, and class and how, separately and in combination, they are interpreted by the wider society. Emphasis on how black and working-class women make sense of their experiences at work and within the family.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Migration and Health
courses.description: This course examines the intersections between migration processes and the political, economic, and social dimensions of health and well-being among migrants, their families, and their communities.

source.text: WGST 445. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER. | ANTH 445 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: American Women Authors
courses.description: American women authors from the beginnings to the present. Honors version available.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender, Space, and Place in the Middle East
courses.description: Examines gender, space, and place relationships in the modern Middle East. Investigates shifting gender geographies of colonialism, nationalism, modernization, and globalization in this region. (GHA)

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Contemporary Judaism
courses.description: The seminar examines the developments in gender roles and in sexuality in contemporary Judaism.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women and Politics in the United States
courses.description: This course examines the history of women's involvement in the political process in the United States from the founding to the present. Students will examine women's historical role in the political process, the different ways that women have engaged as political actors (even when disenfranchised), and the issues that became defined as women's issues.

source.text: WGST 449. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER, FAD. | HIST 449 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Sexuality in Jewish Tradition and History
courses.description: This course deals with various topics related to sexuality and marriage in Jewish tradition and history: sex outside of marriage, wedding ceremonies, regulations of marital sex, menstruation, homosexuality, and more.

source.text: WGST 450. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-VALUES. | RELI 450 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women in the Visual Arts II
courses.description: Discussion of topics related to the representation of women in Western art and/or women as producers of art.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Archaeology of Sex and Gender
courses.description: Required preparation, at least one ANTH or one WMST course. A discussion of gender and sex roles and sexuality in past cultures; a cross-cultural examination of ways of knowing about past human behavior.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender, (Im)migration, and Labor in Latina Literature
courses.description: Students will explore the representation of intersections between gender, identity, immigration, and migration in Latina/o literature. Emphasis will be placed on the intersections between labor, migration, and United States immigration policy.

source.text: WGST 465. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, WGST 101 . | FC-AESTH or FC-GLOBAL.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Middle Eastern Literature
courses.description: We examine gender and sexuality in literature written by various authors from the Middle East. Our discussions will focus on the significance of sexuality, harems, same-sex desire and homosexuality, construction of female sexuality, masculinity, contraception and abortion, the institution of marriage, gay/lesbian underground subcultures, and social media as sexual outlet.

source.text: WGST 471. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER, RESEARCH. | ASIA 471 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Philosophical Issues in Gender, Race, and Class
courses.description: Examines in greater depth and complexity one or more of the issues addressed in PHIL 275 , investigating issues of gender, race, and class within the dominant theories of philosophy.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

source.text: WGST 475. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PHIL 275 or WGST 101 . | PHIL 475 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: History of Feminism
courses.description: This course will examine the unprecedented surge of feminist thought and activism in the postwar United States. Course materials and discussions will trace feminists' varied conceptions of empowered womanhood and their expectations of the state, society at large, and each other. Honors version available.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Advanced Feminist Political Theory
courses.description: Examines in greater depth and complexity current issues in feminist political theory. Topics: theories of subjectivity and solidarity, feminist poststructuralist and post-Marxist thinking, gender in the public sphere.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: History of Female Sexualities
courses.description: Spanning the ancient, medieval, and modern West, this course explores normative and non-normative female sexualities, ideas about female bodies, and the regulation of female sexuality by families, religions, and states.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Queering China
courses.description: This course explores "queer" expressions in Chinese literature and visual culture from 1949 through the twenty-first century. It surveys a combination of all-time classics and lesser-known cultural texts featuring non-heteronormative sexual desire and gender-bending performance. We mobilize queer as a broad site of critique beyond Western models of the concept, asking not only how queer challenges normative bodyminds, but also how it negotiates notions of time, space, affect, and the neoliberal order.

source.text: WGST 480. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER, RESEARCH. | CHIN 480 , CMPL 480 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Sex, Gender, and Religion in South Asia
courses.description: This seminar draws on feminist and philosophical theory, including the works of Plato, Butler, and Foucault, as well as postcolonial theory, to explore the categories of sex and gender in South Asian religions. We also analyze the moral cultivation of the self in relation to gender identity in South Asia.

source.text: WGST 482. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER, RESEARCH. | RELI 482 , ASIA 482 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Exploration of Russian "Women's Prose" and Svetlana Alexievich (Nobel Prize in Literature 2015)
courses.description: Using Alexievich as our beacon, we will explore the writers behind the term "Russian Women's Prose": Valeria Narbikova, Lyudmila Petrushevskaya, Tatyana Tolstaya, and Lyudmila Ulitskaya. The course will delve into gender identity and body politics as they manifest themselves in the literary texts of lasting aesthetic quality and social relevance. Taught in English; some readings in Russian for qualified students.

source.text: WGST 486. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-GLOBAL. | RUSS 486 , EURO 486 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women, Margin, Writing, and Transnational Japan
courses.description: This course explores literary and media art produced by women from various political and social margins of Japan, voiced from their transnational subjectivities. The transnational situations include: immigration, colonialism, diaspora, and international coalition as well as globalizing feminist alliance. By focusing on literature, film, and performance, this course takes an interdisciplinary approach to women's creative political statements.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender, Empire, and Nation
courses.description: This course explores the growing body of research on gender, empire, and nation/nationalism in modern European history by focusing on problems of national belongings and citizenship, state and nation building and empire formation, and the gendered discourses and representations of nation and empire.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender, Culture, and Development
courses.description: Classic writings and debates relating to gender and development, with emphasis on recent work that critiques conventional development models. The scope is global, with special attention to Latin America and to such questions as how alternative approaches to gender, culture, and development may be more inclusive of diverse peoples and grassroots movements for change.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender, Military, and War
courses.description: This course introduces students to new research on the history of gender, the military, and war in a comparative perspective. It explores the interrelations between changing military systems, types of warfare, the gender order, as well as political, social, and cultural currents in modern history.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender, Communication, and Culture
courses.description: Course examines the speeches and other texts that announced and embodied the goals and political strategies of multiple branches of three waves of feminist activism in the United States.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, COMM 224; permission of the instructor for non-majors.

source.text: WGST 524. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, COMM 224 ; permission of the instructor for non-majors. | FC-POWER. | COMM 524 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women, Gender, and Judaism
courses.description: This course examines historical developments in the study of women and gender in Judaism. We will discuss efforts to challenge and revitalize Jewish tradition through the lens of gender theory and other critical interpretive approaches. Topics to be addressed include biblical interpretation, Jewish law, feminist Jewish theology and liturgy, the renewal of ritual, the rabbinic ordination of women, gender identity, race, sexuality, queer, trans, and non-binary approaches, and representations of these themes in various media.

source.text: WGST 533. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-POWER, RESEARCH. | RELI 533 , JWST 533 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women in the Middle East
courses.description: Explores the lives of women in the Middle East and how they have changed over time. Focus will change each year.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Theorizing Black Feminisms
courses.description: Introduction to the theoretical and practical contributions of African American feminists who maintain that issues of race, gender, sexuality, and social class are central, rather than peripheral, to any history or strategy for bringing about social justice in the United States.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, WGST 101 and 202; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites

source.text: WGST 553. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, WGST 101 and 202 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites. | FC-POWER.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women and Creativity
courses.description: This course will present an overview of the variety and diversity of contemporary American women's experiences of creative expressions. We explore how women have been historically excluded from the arts.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, WGST 101 and 202; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites

source.text: WGST 555. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, WGST 101 and 202 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women and Religion in United States History
courses.description: An interdisciplinary consideration of women's roles, behavior, and ideas in the religious life of Americans from 1636 to 1982.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Performance of Women of Color
courses.description: Explores through performance contemporary poetry, fiction, nonfiction, and feminist thought by women of color in the United States. Honors version available.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, COMM 160 or COMM 260 or COMM 263.

source.text: WGST 561. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, COMM 160 or COMM 260 or COMM 263 . | FC-AESTH. | COMM 561 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Oral History and Performance
courses.description: This course combines readings and field work in oral history with the study of performance as a means of interpreting and conveying oral history texts. Honors version available.

source.text: WGST 562. | 3 Credits. | HI-PERFORM. | COMM 562 , FOLK 562 , HIST 562 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women in the South
courses.description: An exploration of the distinctive themes in Southern women's lives, using the evidence of history and literature.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Psychology of Women and Gender
courses.description: This course will discuss theories, methods, and empirical research findings on the physical, cognitive, emotional, and social aspects of the psychology of women, as well as topics such as feminist psychology, intersectionality, bias in psychological research, sexual orientation, sexuality, lifespan development, work, and health. Men and masculinity, the psychology of transgender persons, and a critique of the gender binary are also discussed.

source.text: WGST 573. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PSYC 101 or WGST 101 . | FC-POWER. | PSYC 573 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: The Ethnohistory of Native American Women
courses.description: Introduces students to the study of Native American women through the perspectives of anthropology, history, and autobiography.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender and Imperialism
courses.description: Required preparation, one course in gender or non-Western societies. Permission of the instructor for students lacking the preparation. Focuses on feminist perspectives on imperialism, the effects of imperialism on colonized and European women, women's participation in anti-imperialist movements; and the legacies of imperialism for feminism today.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Women in Hispanic Literature
courses.description: The image of woman in 16th- and 17th-century Hispanic literature. A study of texts by Spanish and Spanish American authors. Readings in Spanish or in English translation. Lectures in English.

source.text: WGST 620. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, SPAN 371 and 373 . | SPAN 620 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender Issues in Planning and Development
courses.description: Permission of the instructor required for undergraduates. Examination of the environmental and health risks, policy institutions, processes, instruments, policy analysis, and major elements of American environmental policy. Lectures and case studies.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Body and Suffering in Christian Mysticism
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. Medieval Christians consistently focused on the suffering body as a means of reflecting on Christ's sacrifice. This course considers how medical theories of cognition, gender, and pain influenced the potential role of the body in medieval mystical experience.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Queer Latina/o Literature, Performance, and Visual Art
courses.description: This course explores literature, performance art, film, and photography by Latinas and Latinos whose works may be described as "queer" and that question terms and norms of cultural dominance.

source.text: WGST 665. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | ENGL 665 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Queer Latina/o Photography and Literature
courses.description: This course explores Latina/o literature about photography in relation to photography by "queer" Latina/o artists and, through this double focus, poses certain questions about identity, subjectivity, and culture.

source.text: WGST 666. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | ENGL 666 .

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Honors in Women's Studies
courses.description: Senior standing and permission of the department. The first semester of the yearlong honors thesis in women's and gender studies. Completing WGST 691H fulfills the WGST 695 requirement for the major.

source.text: WGST 691H. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, WGST 101 and 202 . | RESEARCH.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Honors in Women's Studies
courses.description: Permission of department. Second semester of the yearlong honors thesis project.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Senior Seminar: Principles of Feminist Inquiry
courses.description: Required preparation, at least one additional WGST course and senior standing or permission of the instructor. Required for majors; strongly recommended for minors. An advanced writing-intensive course drawing on a student's interests and background. Major research of specific topics utilizing feminist perspectives. Honors version available.

source.text: WGST 695. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, WGST 101 and 202 . | FC-KNOWING, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Feminism and Society
courses.description: Selected topics in feminist analysis of social life, with materials drawn from a global range of societies.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Selected Readings in the Comparative or Global History of Women and Gender
courses.description: Readings in the history of women and gender in a comparative, global, or transnational perspective.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: French Feminist Theory
courses.description: An introduction to feminist literary theory, focusing on feminist writings from France (in translation) and their sources in psychoanalysis and poststructuralism. Anglo-American counterparts and adaptations of the French theorists in the United States will also be treated.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Feminist and Gender Theory for Historians
courses.description: Readings in contemporary feminist and gender theory, focused especially on theories that address the construction, writing, and general practice of history.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Readings in the History of Sexuality and Gender
courses.description: Readings on the historical study of gender and sexuality and on definitions of femininity and masculinity in different historical contexts.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender, Sickness, and Society
courses.description: This seminar deals in depth and cross-culturally with the nature of gender and the ways in which social comprehension of gender, gender status, and gender relationships impinge upon differential experience of health and sickness of men and women from a historical and contemporary perspective.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Readings in Medieval and Early Modern Women's History
courses.description: A readings course on the history of women, gender, and sexuality in Medieval Europe.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Feminist Political Theory
courses.description: A survey of feminist approaches to politics and political inquiry.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Readings in Modern European Women's and Gender History
courses.description: A readings course in the history of women in Europe since 1500.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender, Race, and Class Issues in Education
courses.description: Provides an understanding of (and remedies for) the racism, sexism, and class divisions that schools can perpetuate. Examines curriculum, counseling, and interaction in classrooms; structure and leadership; and fundamental assumptions.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Gender, Policy, and Leadership in Education
courses.description: Covers feminist critiques of organizational and political power structures in readings and discussions leading to group and individual research projects.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Graduate Seminar in Women's Studies
courses.description: Explores the complex interaction between women's studies, feminist studies and gender studies as these fields have evolved within and across academic disciplines, intersecting with issues of race, class, ethnicity, masculinity, sexuality, and with practices of queer theory and cultural studies.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Graduate Independent Reading and Research
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Intensive reading and research in a student's chosen area of interest under faculty supervision. Results in a written report.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Critical Ethnic Studies (CES): New Perspectives
courses.description: This course is devised to provide graduate students interested in theoretical interdisciplinary work with a sense of prevailing questions and critiques important to CES. CES takes on the more difficult questions of intersectional work, as it thinks through sovereignty and emancipation, identity and ontology, place, space and temporality. Each iteration of the course works itself through new perspectives in the field, challenging students to create new methodologies for their own work.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Sociology of Gender
courses.description: Reviews theory on variation in men's and women's gender roles, with emphasis on industrialized societies and women's roles.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Seminar in Feminist Studies of Film and Television
courses.description: Graduate standing required. This graduate seminar explores theoretical and practical points of contact between feminism, film, and television using psychoanalysis, narrative analysis, ideological analysis, and cultural studies.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Readings in United States Women's and Gender History
courses.description: A readings course on the history of women and gender in the United States.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Topics in Women's Studies
courses.description: This course allows faculty in WMST to offer graduate-level courses on special topics pertinent to their current research.

courses.subject: WGST
courses.title: Seminar in Women's and Gender History
courses.description: Writing seminar for graduate students on all levels who work on the history of women and gender.
